turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Hi Mrs. Nguyen, I'm the nurse from the home health agency. This is your start of care visit, so I'll be asking a lot of questions today.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Who sets up your pills? How do you keep track of them?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You take the right pills only when someone reminds you at the right time.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: I have to ask some history questions — any falls, hospital stays, ER visits this year?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I fell twice since the summer.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I've been in the hospital twice in the last few months.

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER (neighbor)
turns.text: She's been a lot more confused and down these past couple of months.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: That's eight pills a day total.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm just exhausted all the time.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My weight's been steady.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My grandson's coming by Saturday, he's starting college.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How do you get in and out of bed, or from the bed to your chair?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You can bear weight and pivot, but you needed a lot of help from me to finish the transfer.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: And from the waist down — pants, socks, shoes?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can't bend to get my socks or shoes on, somebody has to help me with that and with my pants.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Any trouble with the toilet?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You're using the bedside commode since you can't get to the bathroom.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you stand up from the chair for me?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My neighbor helps some, but I do most of the work to stand up from the chair.

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER (neighbor)
turns.text: Do you want some coffee? I just made a pot.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: After you use the toilet, can you clean yourself and fix your clothes?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With cleaning up after toileting, I helped, but you did more than half of the effort.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you walk over to the doorway for me? About ten feet.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My neighbor helps some, but I do most of the work to walk about ten feet, like over to the kitchen.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How about eating — can you feed yourself?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: When it came to feeding yourself, you did it completely by yourself, no help from me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How are you bathing right now?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You can wash yourself, but someone has to be with you the entire time you're in the shower.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How are you managing with washing your face, brushing your teeth, combing your hair?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: If somebody puts my comb and toothbrush on the tray table, I can do it myself. I just can't get them from the bathroom.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Let's see you go from lying down to sitting on the edge of the bed.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Once my neighbor puts the bed rail up, I sit up on the side of the bed from lying down on my own.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you get your shirt on these days?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You needed me to guide your right arm into the sleeve and do the buttons.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: And brushing your teeth or cleaning your dentures?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Once my neighbor puts the toothpaste on the brush and fills the cup, I brush my teeth on my own.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Let's talk about walking.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can only walk if someone is right next to me holding on to me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Now let's try bed to chair.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With the bed-to-chair transfer, I helped, but you did more than half of the effort.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How's your breathing been?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You get short of breath walking longer distances or on the stairs.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Over the past five days, how often has pain made it hard for you to sleep at night?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Rarely. The pain hardly ever keeps me up.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Okay, that's everything for today. I'll see you Thursday.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: For feeding yourself, I only set things up; after that you did it on your own.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Your blood pressure is 138 over 82, pulse 76, oxygen 95 percent.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you stand up from the chair for me?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With standing up from the chair, I did most of the effort; you helped a little.

turns.text: Do you want some coffee? I just you know, made a pot.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you walk over to the doorway for me? About ten feet.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: We're not going to attempt walking the ten feet to the doorway today, it isn't safe with your condition.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Let's see you go from lying down to sitting on the edge of the bed.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With going from lying to sitting on the edge of the bed, I helped, but you did more than half of the effort.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: And brushing your teeth or cleaning your dentures?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With brushing your teeth, I helped, but you did more than half of the effort.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Tell me how showers are going.

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER (son)
turns.text: She can't use the tub, but she gives herself a sponge bath at the sink on her own.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How's your breathing been?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I get winded just getting dressed or walking to the bathroom.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Over the past five days, how often has pain made it hard for you to sleep at night?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Almost constantly. I barely sleep at all because of the pain.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Okay, that's everything for today. I'll see you Thursday.

turns.text: Who sets up your pills? How do you keep track of them?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You take the right pills only when someone reminds you at the right time.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: The TV's loud, let me turn it down.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: I have to ask some history questions — any falls, hospital stays, ER visits this year?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I fell twice since the summer.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I've lost about twelve pounds this year without even trying.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I've been in the hospital twice in the last few months.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: We've been to the emergency room three times since August.

turns.speaker: CAREGIVER (granddaughter)
turns.text: She's been a lot more confused and down these past couple of months.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Honestly I don't always take my water pill, and I don't really stick to the diet.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: That's eight pills a day total.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My grandson's coming by Saturday, he's starting college.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: And brushing your teeth or cleaning your dentures?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: For brushing your teeth, you did it yourself with me just steadying you and giving cues.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: And from the waist down — pants, socks, shoes?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You got your pants over your feet but I had to pull them up and put on your socks and shoes.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How are you getting around the house? Any stairs?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can only walk if someone is right next to me holding on to me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Tell me about your morning routine at the sink.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You started washing your face but I had to help you finish and comb the back of your hair.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Let's see you go from lying down to sitting on the edge of the bed.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I sit up on the side of the bed from lying down myself, but my granddaughter has to stand right there and steady me or remind me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How about eating — can you feed yourself?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: When it came to feeding yourself, you did it completely by yourself, no help from me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Any trouble with the toilet?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I can't get to the toilet or the commode. I use the bedpan, and I can manage it myself.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How are you bathing right now?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You can wash yourself, but someone has to be with you the entire time you're in the shower.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How about getting dressed up top — shirts, buttons, your bra or undershirt?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Buttons are the problem, somebody has to do them and help with the sleeves.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How do you get in and out of bed, or from the bed to your chair?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You can bear weight and pivot, but you needed a lot of help from me to finish the transfer.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you walk over to the doorway for me? About ten feet.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: For walking the ten feet to the doorway, you did it yourself with me just steadying you and giving cues.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Now let's try bed to chair.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My granddaughter helps some, but I do most of the work to get from the bed into my chair.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Can you stand up from the chair for me?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: My granddaughter helps some, but I do most of the work to stand up from the chair.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: After you use the toilet, can you clean yourself and fix your clothes?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: With cleaning up after toileting, I helped, but you did more than half of the effort.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: How's your breathing been?

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: You were short of breath just while talking with me.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Over the past five days, how often has pain made it hard for you to sleep at night?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Rarely. The pain hardly ever keeps me up.

turns.speaker: NURSE
turns.text: Okay, that's everything for today. I'll see you Thursday.

turns.text: And brushing your teeth or cleaning your dentures?
